fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles to allow fire apparatus and emergency vehicles to reach both structures.
• Identify and mark a designated turnaround area near the main residence or detached structure so drivers can reverse out without blocking the access drive.
• Post the address visibly at the single access point so responding units can confirm the correct property without delay.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clearance wide enough for emergency vehicles on both sides.
• Cut back overhanging branches along the drive to maintain vertical clearance for ladder trucks and tall apparatus.
• Clear a path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings on foot without pushing through dense plantings.
• Mark the location of the solar system shutoff or rapid shutdown device on the exterior of the residence so arriving crews can locate it without searching.
• Keep a gate or pathway on at least one side of the main residence unlocked and clear so responders can reach the rear of the structure without passing through the interior.
• Thin dense vegetation near both structures so responders have room to work, stage equipment, and move safely around the buildings.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim lower branches on the large trees closest to the structure to reduce the path fire can travel from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Thin the tree cluster to create more open space between individual trees, reducing how easily fire can spread from one tree to the next.
• Remove any shrubs or ground-level plants growing directly against or touching the structure.
• Clear dead leaves, needles, and small branches that have collected on the ground beneath the scattered trees near the structure.
• Keep the area under and around the tree cluster free of accumulated dead plant material on the ground.
• Maintain the open terrain around the structure by preventing new shrub or brush growth from establishing close to the building.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches and low vegetation so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
